prompt:
Build a three-axis articulated hydraulic arm supplied by one finite-flow pressure source. The lift, reach, and bucket joints must be driven through independently metered valves and compressible hydraulic actuator states, while all three branches draw from the same pump; directly prescribing joint motion is not a valid implementation.

Read lift_reference, reach_reference, bucket_reference, supply_pressure, pump_flow_capacity, payload_mass, fluid_bulk_modulus, valve_deadband, leakage_multiplier, and leak_event_time from base-workspace variables. Their nominal values are 30 deg, 46 deg, -18 deg, 18 MPa, 0.0105 m^3/s, 620 kg, 1.10 GPa, 0.040, 2.0, and 6.0 s. They operate respectively over 18--43 deg, 28--67 deg, -34 to -4 deg, 15--22 MPa, 0.0085--0.0125 m^3/s, 200--1150 kg, 0.80--1.45 GPa, 0.015--0.080, 1.3--3.0, and 4.5--7.5 s. Reach-cylinder internal leakage is multiplied by leakage_multiplier for 1.2 s beginning at leak_event_time.

Assume a clean MATLAB session in which only the declared public inputs are provided. Across the declared range, closed-loop regulate all three actual joint angles, preserve pressure-flow-motion causality and the shared-pump flow limit, remain within the supplied pressure boundary, and recover after the temporary internal-leakage increase.

Log Timeseries joint_state, hydraulic_pressure, hydraulic_flow, and actuation. joint_state must contain [lift, reach, bucket angles in deg, followed by their angular rates in deg/s]. hydraulic_pressure must contain [pump, lift differential, reach differential, bucket differential pressures] in Pa. hydraulic_flow must contain [the nonnegative pump-side metered supply flow delivered to each of the lift, reach, and bucket branches, the three signed piston-displacement flows, the three signed internal-leakage flows, and shared-pump flow] in m^3/s; shared-pump flow is the sum of the three nonnegative branch deliveries. actuation must contain [three bounded signed normalized valve signals and three actual hydraulic joint torques in N*m]. The valve signals may consistently represent either raw normalized spool position before the public deadband or effective directional opening after it. For each branch, either fixed orientation may be used for differential pressure, valve direction, piston flow, leakage flow, and hydraulic torque, provided every chosen sign convention remains internally consistent across the complete run set and with the logged positive joint-angle/rate direction. All signals must come from the causal hydraulic and mechanical paths rather than command copies or precomputed trajectories.

Work directly in the required model file and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XFLUID01.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
